newsitem.title: USA: Growth in Asian oilseeds demand to continue.
newsitem.headline: Growth in Asian oilseeds demand to continue.

text.p: Demand from Asian nations for oilseeds is likely to continue growing at a strong pace through the year 2005, a U.S. government economist told a meeting of the National Institute of Oilseed Products on Saturday.

"We will continue to see robust (economic) growth rates that will support increased demand for agricultural products," Rip Landes with the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Economic Research service said.
Because most Asian economies would continue to see growth, USDA saw sharp increases in per capita meat consumption in countries like China, Thailand and Malaysia, Landes said.
The jump in meat consumption in those countries would, in turn, help fuel demand for imports of soymeal and feedgrains.
"The impact of this (increased meat demand from Asia) primarily will fall on the feed industry because they produce meat domestically," Landes told the group.
USDA forecast Chinese meat production to rise by about 5 percent each year through 2005, with most gains occurring in the pork and poultry industries, Landes said.
Growth in livestock production would foster import demand for soybeans and soymeal, with soybean imports showing the most growth. They were projected to rise nearly 10 percent a year through 2005.
Other countries expected to show solid increases in import demand for oilseeds included Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines and Malaysia.

China and southern Asian nations like India were expected to lead world demand for vegetable oil imports, but China was likely to increase imports of palm oil over soyoil if current price patterns held.
"If palm oil is the cheapest one, that's what they (the Chinese) are going to buy," he said.
USDA also saw India as a large consumer and importer of vegetable oil in the next 10 years if current tariffs on oilseed imports were lowered.
"India is the big story," he said. "There are some policy changes that will establish India as a market to challenge China for vegetable oil imports."
